JRA - THE DEMISE OF A CITY’s ROADS

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The City of Johannesburg’s road infrastructure appears to crumbling, we expose a trail of alleged political interference that seems to steering the demise.

Unique Selling Point:
No one else has this scoop – we are teaming up with Amabhungane to expose alleged corruption within the Johannesburg Roads Agency.


Summary:
Johannesburg Residents are all too aware of the shocking state of the city’s roads, with an increase in potholes, broken traffic lights and seemingly non-existent maintenance. The reasons behind the demise of the Johannesburg Roads Agency is a lot more sinister than meets the eye.

Political interference under the guise of protecting coalitions are attempting to steer tender allocation processes and has resulted in the mass exodus of JRA top management.

We lift the lid on the JRA road to corruption.

Further information:
The JRA used to be an effective department within the City of Jo’burg spending it’s allocated budgets widely and delivering an improved road infrastructure to it’s residents. But since the Democratic Alliance has taken over control of Johannesburg, it appears that things have gone backwards.

The MD has resigned. The company secretary has resigned. The Head of Engineering has resigned. All in protest of the current interference.

The DA has a coalition arrangement with the IFP who appears to have an increased presence within the JRA. The new MMC for Roads & Transport is an IFP representative – Nonhlanhla Makhuba. It is alleged that the new JRA board was hand picked by the IFP.

Enter new chairman Sipho Tshabalala. He approached the JRA MD Sean Williams demanding that the MD is “not to award any tenders without involving him in the decision making”. Not only is the unethical business practice…. This is illegal in terms of the Municipal Finance Management Act.

The board also moved to establish a news Project Management Unit which would invole the appointment of a firm of consultants to manage some of the key procurement processed related to capital works and manage the implementation of capital works. THE JRA ALREADY HAS AN EXISTING INTERNAL DEPARTMENT HANDLING THIS.

After the company secretary did a protected disclosure exposing these irregularities amongst others – she was suspended – she was later paid out to leave – no action taken after she challenged her suspension legally.

The MD Sean Williams raised the issues with Mayor Herman Mashaba – he has done nothing. The MD resigned shortly after the Company Secretary was suspended.

AFTER THE MASS EXODUS….

The M1 Double Decker contract – RED FLAG!
- the contract was given to White Hazy Construction – they only did 7% of the work despite the project running over the deadline and received around 40% of the project fee.
- The project has now been awarded to Khato Civils – a controversial company involved in the Lesotho Highlands Project for almost double the original contract.
- BUT THE BIGGEST RED FLAG…. A Pre-Payment was made in December 2017 of R17million!! Despite resistance from key JRA finance department officials.

- MICAH REDDY – AMABHUNGANE JOURNALIST
- SEAN WILLIAM – FORMER MD
- JRA chairman – SIPHO TSHABALA

Press Release:



The Road Paved With Potholes
The City of Johannesburg’s road infrastructure seems to be in a serious state of disrepair with a marked increase in potholes, broken traffic lights and a general lack of maintenance. What’s behind the shocking state of Johannesburg’s roads? Carte Blanche investigates a trail of alleged political interference in contracts that may to be steering the demise.


Script:


STRUCTURE JRA

VO: The City of Johannesburg’s road infrastructure appears to be crumbling, with the organization’s performance record at an all time low.

Six months ago, before the rains, the city’s State Of Roads Infrastructure report stated that, just 45 % of the city’s roads, were considered to be in a very good condition.

And the city’s road users, are not impressed.

VOX 1: Driving in GP is a nightmare these days, the roads are deteriorating
VOX: We’ve got the potholes, most of the traffic lights are not working – some are taking a week before they get fixed.
VOX 2: They are absolutely shocking and they’ve gotten worse

VO: The DA took the City of Joburg administration from the ANC in the 2016 Municipal Elections – retaining power through coalition partnerships with smaller political parties.

Herman Mashaba is the Mayor.

HERMAN: /As you expect the new administration to turn around the city in 18 months – we are not magicians – it’s going to take some time //I1m11

VO: But Mayor Mashaba, in the time you’ve been in office, it’s gotten worse.

Political Analyst Ralph Mathekga attributes service delivery issues to coalition agreements in government.

RALPH I call it a pay as you go arrangement – every time you want to make a decision in council, or any government that is made out of a coalition – you have to buy airtime.

VO: The Johannesburg Roads Agency falls under the city’s transport department, which has been assigned to the Inkatha Freedom Party - one of the DA’s coalition partners.

Insiders at the JRA say, the organization has been bleeding top management since the new board took office - with 6 of the 10 executives leaving the organization in the last year.

Amabhungane Journalist Micah Reddy picked up on the story in late 2017 – he says some of the exiting high level staff, felt that there was politics at play within the JRA.

MICAH: They were saying at heart is new IFP aligned board – that came in after local gov elections – that the board is overbearing – trying to involve in tenders, insisting in non performing contractor against the wishes of MD who wanted them gone I1M2

VO: The Joburg M1 Double Decker Bridge project kicked off in 2015.

This was set for R91 million upgrade and the contract was awarded to White Hazy Construction – a Mpumalanga based company.

LINK: Over two years into the project the deadline was missed and only 17% of the project was completed.

MICAH: the contractor was massively under prefomring //. I1M4 // the board would not have the cancellation earlier on and the board and the CFO clearly moved against it – it’s clear in the minutes. // I2M10

VO: And it seems, that the power struggles within the JRA were becoming more intense by the day.

LINK: The company secretary and ethics officer, Karen Mills was the first executive casualty at the JRA, she was suspended for making a protected disclosure – she was removed from office for blowing the whistle on what she believed was questionable governance.

VO: The Board became aware of the protected disclosure and claimed that Karen didn’t follow procedure.

Karen now lives in the UK and spoke to us via Skype.

KAREN: ……failed to be complied with the board directive that I not speak to the shareholder which is the city of jhb or the independent audit committee or anyone else M13

VO: Short of reporting it to herself, as the ethics & compliance officer, Karen said she took all the steps that were available to her. Reddy believes Karen Mills was the most worrying departure from the JRA.

MICAH: The protected disclosure Sent to General Sibiya – mayor’s anti corruption tsar //. I4M3 //it appears that her disclosure was intercepted and used to discipline her and ultimately push her out of the company. I3M8

VO: With no formal disciplinary hearing, Karen was eventually paid a sizable settlement amount to resign and just leave.

KAREN: The irony is that I was put through 7 months of hell before I was given the boot for doing my job and again I didn’t accuse anybody of anything – I raised my concerns

VO: Next in the firing line, was the then MD, Dr Sean Phillips, who had a somewhat strained relationship with the JRA board chairman – SIPHO TSHABALALA.

SEAN: The problem started because the chairman of the board came to see me at my office to talk to me about the governance of the agency and the role of the board and one issue that he stressed he wanted to be involved in the award of tenders I1M10
DEVI: What was your reaction?
SEAN: I was shocked // – I told him it’s illegal in terms of the MFMA I1M10 //he reacted by saying I must involve him informally. I1M11

VO: We put Dr Phillips allegations to the JRA Chairman.

DEVI: What’s your response SP
SIPHO: that’s not true - m1
DEVI: Do you think SP is lying?
SIPHO: Yes
DEVI: Why is he lying?
SIPHO: I don’t know I am not SP M4

VO: With a doctorate in Civil Engineering which focused on Roads, and two masters degrees – Dr Phillips was concerned about corporate governance related to tender allocations and the Karen Mills case. He formally raised it with Mayor Mashaba.

The Mayor then facilitated a meeting between Dr Phillips and the Chairman Mr Tshabalala, who said it was all a misunderstanding and apologized for any confusion.

Mayor Mashaba was adamant that he can’t and won’t take any other action without concrete evidence of wrongdoing.

DEVI: Why SP stick neck out –
HERMAN: // I don’t work on the basis of trusting people just because they are MDs – I work on trusting evidence // i1m32

SEAN you can’t wait for corruption to occur before acting against it// – I think it was my duty to raise concerns about governance problems that could lead to corruption. I1M35

VO: Political analyst Ralph Mathekga is not surprised by how it played out.

RALPH When you are engaged in coalitions, you are walking on eggshells, particularly when you share nothing concrete with the people you are in a coalition with. // the only thing Mr Mashaba can do is look the other way –// I1M24

VO: The problematic M1 contract was eventually cancelled. Enter a new company - Khato Civils, this time at a price tag of R144 and a half million excluding VAT.

LINK: // Even if we take into consideration that there was probably more deterioration, that there would have been price increases and even possible miscalculations – but for the contract value to double? Something doesn’t sound right.

MICAH: They don’t go out to tender, bring in this Khato Civils this new company on an emergency tender, and they give them an upfront payment // I2M1

VO: Yes, you heard right… an upfront payment of R22 million was made to Khato Civils in December 2017, while the project documentation was only finalised in February 2018.

Money was paid before work was done. We shared our discovery with Mayor Mashaba.

DEVI: Is pre-payment normal?
HERMAN: can not be normal.
DEVI: Let me show you….. i2m16 // take your time with this… khato civils….
HERMAN…. 5 million… 5, 5…. Payment dates…. I2m17
DEVI: They said it was an emergency
HERMAN: you are getting rid of one construction company that was under preforming and get another one and you pay them in advance – that’s nonsense – it cant be…i2m19

VO: But it is.

Despite the JRA officially responding extensively to AmaBhungane’s questions - responses which we have seen - when we sat down with the acting MD, Goodwill Mbatha – it was Lights, camera & no comment…

The Acting MD had no comment – 27 times.

UPSOUND NO COMMENT….

VO: Apparently the Special Investigations Unit has told the JRA not to comment pending an investigation that started months ago.

D: How is that you were able to comment to Amabhungane extensively but you cant talk to us?
GW: I was only advised today at about 10:00 that I shouldn’t comment on the matter….
D: it’s a bit coincidental isn’t?
GW: it is coincidental – the meeting were set up quite a while ago… M34
D: Why did you pay KC a 22 million prepayment? It has been admitted to already by the JRA – not if, it’s WHY?
GW: I would comment on that because there are reasons why actions are taken, but because of the restriction I am unable to comment any further on that matter M44
D: You admitted to amaB that it is a prepayment – you guys have not been shy about it – you are trying to close the door, the horse is gone. That’s what’s happening here. // M43

VO: Reddy explains that any advance payments for private contractors are highly irregular.

MICAH: // We’ve spoken to governance experts, people in public entities who say that prepayments are avoided like the plague…. //I2M12

DEVI: how many prepayments were approved in your time as MD
SEAN NONE! I2M12
DEVI: Are prepayments common in municipal organisations like the JRA? I2M8
SEAN no, it’s not normal//it is very rare to be given a prepayment - as far as I concerned it’s unheard of I2M11

VO: It seems the JRA is trying to manipulate procedures to get around legislation.

DE: Law not allowed, govern expert not allowed, treasury standards not allowed… mayor says not allowed – is everyone mad?
GW: what is not allowed to make a payment for services that have not been rendered and make as if those services had been rendered….but if by agreement there is a payment plan
D: why did they need a payment plan –they are a big company?
GW: they need a payment plan – but I can’t comment further on that. M51

VO: However, Khato Civils did respond, saying it “did not receive an “advance payment” we were paid part of the contracts’ preliminary and generals (P&Gs)”.

They go on to say: “It is not for Khato Civils to comment on the procurement and payment processes in JRA, we are merely a contractor who was awarded a tender and are carrying out our contractual obligations.”

VO: Political analyst Mathekga points out that there are more opportunities for corruption in the local government context, simply because of the magnitude of transactions.

RALPH // – most of the money is actually spent at local government – those cities are going to be a strategic area for patronage as these coalitions are being made. I1M27

LINK: While political party funding is not transparent - it is impossible to say where the money went, if it went anywhere, but what is glaringly clear that a board of a municipal entity should not be getting involved with the day-to-day operations of the organisation.

KAREN: Pravin GOrdan…. This for me was it….// M18

MICAH: I think it dispels this myth that the ANC is the party of corruption, here we have a very messy coalition that in a sense may be fuelling corruption in the city’s entitites I5M15

VO: But at the end of the day the buck stops with Mayor Mashaba.

HERMAN: I take full accountability for running of city i1m7



PROMOS
PROMO 1
We lift the lid on the Johannesburg Roads Agency’s crumblilng road system, where it seems questionable management decisions are being made under a DA-led coalition administration.

PROMO 2
While Joburg roads are deteriorating rapidly there seems to be a mass exodus of top management at the Johannesburg Roads Agency.

KAREN: The irony is that I was put through 7 months of hell before I was given the boot for doing my job



PROMO 3
VO: We ask if political coalitions could be driving seemingly questionable management decisions that are being made in municipal entities like the Johannesburg Roads Agency.

RALPH // –those cities are going to be a strategic area for patronage as these coalitions are being made. I1M27


PROMO 4
VO: We uncover seemingly irregular payments at the Johannesburg Roads Agency totalling millions of rands - we break the news to Mayor Mashaba.

dEVI First time you hearing?
HERMAN: Yes…
DEVI: Is pre-payment normal?
HERMAN: can not be normal.
DEVI: they said it was an emergency
HERMAN: you are // and you pay them in advance – that’s nonsense – it cant be…i2m19

VO: Could political alliances be steering questionable management decisions?

We investigate

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The City of Johannesburg’s road infrastructure appears to crumbling, we expose a trail of alleged political interference that seems to steering the demise.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: No one else has this scoop – we are teaming up with Amabhungane to expose alleged corruption within the Johannesburg Roads Agency.
metadata.Summary: Johannesburg Residents are all too aware of the shocking state of the city’s roads, with an increase in potholes, broken traffic lights and seemingly non-existent maintenance. The reasons behind the demise of the Johannesburg Roads Agency is a lot more sinister than meets the eye. Political interference under the guise of protecting coalitions are attempting to steer tender allocation processes and has resulted in the mass exodus of JRA top management. We lift the lid on the JRA road to corruption.
metadata.Further information: The JRA used to be an effective department within the City of Jo’burg spending it’s allocated budgets widely and delivering an improved road infrastructure to it’s residents. But since the Democratic Alliance has taken over control of Johannesburg, it appears that things have gone backwards. The MD has resigned. The company secretary has resigned. The Head of Engineering has resigned. All in protest of the current interference. The DA has a coalition arrangement with the IFP who appears to have an increased presence within the JRA. The new MMC for Roads & Transport is an IFP representative – Nonhlanhla Makhuba. It is alleged that the new JRA board was hand picked by the IFP. Enter new chairman Sipho Tshabalala. He approached the JRA MD Sean Williams demanding that the MD is “not to award any tenders without involving him in the decision making”. Not only is the unethical business practice…. This is illegal in terms of the Municipal Finance Management Act. The board also moved to establish a news Project Management Unit which would invole the appointment of a firm of consultants to manage some of the key procurement processed related to capital works and manage the implementation of capital works. THE JRA ALREADY HAS AN EXISTING INTERNAL DEPARTMENT HANDLING THIS. After the company secretary did a protected disclosure exposing these irregularities amongst others – she was suspended – she was later paid out to leave – no action taken after she challenged her suspension legally. The MD Sean Williams raised the issues with Mayor Herman Mashaba – he has done nothing. The MD resigned shortly after the Company Secretary was suspended. AFTER THE MASS EXODUS…. The M1 Double Decker contract – RED FLAG! - the contract was given to White Hazy Construction – they only did 7% of the work despite the project running over the deadline and received around 40% of the project fee. - The project has now been awarded to Khato Civils – a controversial company involved in the Lesotho Highlands Project for almost double the original contract. - BUT THE BIGGEST RED FLAG…. A Pre-Payment was made in December 2017 of R17million!! Despite resistance from key JRA finance department officials.
